claim: Part I leaves the equivocation wedge (I9) fully open while §0 claims it 'closes the malicious wedge'
sections: 0, 3.4, 4 (exit criterion), 11 Stage 1 gate
attacks: n=4 {A,B,C,D}; D holds one validator key. (1) Round r: D sends twin T1 to A and B and twin T2 to C (asymmetric delivery, the I9 scenario). On A and B the later-arriving T2 hits the equivocation branch (dag.rs:1132-1160): slash proof broadcast, return without insert; the sys:equiv_seen latch (dag.rs:2287-2290) means T2 is never admitted on A/B, and symmetrically T1 never on C. Part I has no shadow and no fetch. (2) Round r+1: A_{r+1}, B_{r+1} cite T1 (resolved on A, B); C_{r+1} cites T2; D withholds its own vote or cites T2. (3) Round r+2 on A: resolve_walk(C_{r+1}) -> edge to T2 -> not in dag, not committed, never admissible -> Unresolved forever; resolve_walk(D_{r+1}) likewise. A resolves {A,B}_{r+1} = 50% -> R4 refuses. B same. C resolves {C,D}_{r+1} = 50% -> refuses. (4) No vertex is ever produced at r+2 or later on any node; no votes for L_r (50% at most); no anchor, no block, no adoption. Permanent halt of the whole network from one key, no fake hash needed. This is the same attacker capability (one validator key) that section 3.4 says Part I neutralises; the outcome equals HEAD's commit wedge, but Part I moves it to the proposer so the only Part I recovery path (adopt_synced_anchor, dag.rs:2871-2878) can never fire, and none of the Part I gates (rows 1-7, 48 h honest burn-in) exercise it. Part I is therefore not 'shippable alone' against the threat it names in section 0.

n = 4 (X attacker, N1, N2, N3). X sends twin A_r to N1 and twin B_r to N2, N3 (direct TCP to chosen peers, or just gossip race). At ingress the second-arriving twin on each node is dropped without insertion and every redelivery is dropped again (dag.rs:1139-1170: equivocation branch returns before persist/insert) — unchanged by Part I. Round r+1: N1's resolved round-r candidates are [A, N1_r, N2_r, N3_r] → cites all (4/4); N2, N3 cite [B, …]. Round r+2: on N1, N2_{r+1} and N3_{r+1} cite B ∉ dag, ∉ committed_set → Unresolved; N1's cited stake = {N1, X} = 2/4 → R4 fails → no proposal. On N2/N3, N1_{r+1} cites A → Unresolved → cited stake {N2, N3} = 2/4 → R4 fails. All honest proposers stop; re-gossip (dag.rs:881-926) redelivers A to N2 which drops it as equivocation again. No anchor ever commits (there is no block for sync to adopt); apply_equivocation_slash writes only local rows (validator:jailed / sys:equiv_seen), never sys:validator_set:v1 (executor-only), so X's stake stays in the denominator. Permanent halt, no fetch could help even if it existed because the twin is rejected at ingress. At HEAD the same key wedges commit_one_anchor instead (I9) — Part I neither worsens nor closes it, yet §0 says Part I 'closes the malicious wedge' and §11 gates Stage 1 shipping on Part I alone. Part I is shippable only as 'closes the fake-parent wedge; equivocation halt still one key away'.
fixes: Either state in section 0/11 that Stage 1 does not close single-key halts and that mainnet is gated on Stage 2-4, or pull the bounded shadow STORE of section 6 (one compact+parents row per (author, round), written after guards drop, read by resolve_walk as dag ∪ shadow) into Stage 1 without E1/E2, so both twins are resolvable on every node that receives both, and make the leader-round decision defer (not skip, not commit) whenever leader_vertex_hash finds more than one twin. Add a Part I adversarial row 'equivocation_2_2_does_not_stop_proposing' with the mutation 'drop the second twin at ingress'.

Either (a) move the minimal shadow store (§6: one compact+parents row per (author, round), loaded at boot, read by resolve_walk over dag ∪ shadow, never in round_index) into Part I so a citation of either twin resolves once both are held — this needs no messages, only a second ingress path for the counterpart body; or (b) state in §0/§11 that Part I does NOT close B3/B4 and cannot ship as the closure, and put the I9 test (twins split 2:2 and 3:1 with Part I only; assert the chain keeps committing) into Part I's gate. Either way add the row with mutation 'drop the second twin at ingress'.
titles: Part I claims to close the malicious wedge, but one equivocating key still halts the chain permanently, now at the proposer where ChainSync cannot rescue it

Part I leaves the audit-119 equivocation wedge (I9) as a one-key permanent halt while §0 claims Part I 'closes the malicious wedge' and is shippable alone; R4 turns the asymmetric split into a symmetric proposal halt

claim: Timestamp future-drift (dag.rs:980-991) is a node-local hard DROP, not a deferral: the same signed vertex is admitted on one node and dropped on another
sections: §3.3 ('the existing 12 checks' as pure functions of bytes), §12 ('Timestamp future-drift i
attacks: dag.rs:980-991: `if vertex.timestamp > now + 30 { return; }` — `now` is the receiver's wall clock; the vertex is discarded before dedup, not parked. §3.3 lists this among the '12 checks' that are 'a pure function of bytes' and §12 says 'deferral, retried' — both false at HEAD. Attack (needs a validator key, same threat model as the B3/B4 wedge Part I claims to close): A emits V_r with timestamp = now_A + 29 s and valid parents. Honest B whose clock is ≥ now_A − 1 s admits V_r; C and D whose clocks are ≥ 1 s behind A reject it (ordinary NTP spread). B_{r+1} cites [A,B,C,D]_r and resolves fine on B. On C: resolve_walk(B_{r+1}) -> V_r absent -> Unresolved{V_r}; nothing will re-deliver V_r: gossipsub's message-id cache suppresses the identical bytes for 60 s (p2p.rs:119-123), and the only re-push is the below-quorum loop (dag.rs:881-926) which sends dag.values() of a STUCK node — C and D do not hold V_r. C, D at r+2 can cite only [C,D]_{r+1} -> 2/4 not > 2/3 -> they do not propose (R4, §3.1). B at r+3 sees only A_{r+2}, B_{r+2} -> B stops too. All honest proposing stops until B itself falls below quorum and re-pushes V_r (round window ≥ current−3) AND the 60 s dedup on C/D has expired — a multi-round stall per attacker vertex, repeatable every round A is entitled to propose, so sustained throughput collapses to roughly one round per dedup window. After the set shrinks to 3 active validators (post-slash), quorum needs all three: one rejecting node is enough to freeze proposals entirely until the re-push lands. The design's I1 argument in §3.4 ('every honest vertex cites > 2/3 so the skip premise holds') silently assumes honest nodes agree on what was admitted; this check guarantees they do not.
fixes: Remove the wall-clock predicate from ingress. Either (a) bound the timestamp against a deterministic quantity every node agrees on — the BFT block time of the latest committed block (blockchain::bft_block_timestamp, already used for headers) plus a fixed protocol slack, which is a pure function of the committed chain — or (b) keep the wall-clock bound but express it as a walk-edge Deferred verdict (Unresolved{blocked_on: time@ts}) with the body ADMITTED and held in dag, released by the tick re-walk once local `now` passes ts − 30 s; the vertex is then cited by everyone or by no one at the same logical point. In both cases the design must state that no ingress `return` may depend on the receiver's clock, and add a test row: A emits ts = now+29 s, receivers skewed ±2 s; assert identical citation sets and no proposer stall; mutation = restore the ingress drop.
titles: Timestamp future-drift check is a node-local hard DROP, not the 'deferral' §12 claims; a 29 s-future vertex splits honest admission by clock skew and, post-slash with 3 active validators, stalls the chain for every round the attacker chooses

claim: Stage 1's exit criterion is vacuously satisfiable and two test rows require a delivery Part I cannot perform
sections: 10 row 3, 4 (exit criterion)
§4 exit criterion, §10 'live' row; api_local.rs:2119-2148, :903-920; sync/src/lib.rs:928-1
§4 exit criterion, §10 rows 3 and 8, §11 Stage 1 gate; dag.rs:881-926, :2852-2884; p2p.rs:
attacks: §4's criterion is 'byte-identical committed sequences and identical anchor_hash per height on every node'. The only per-height RPC surface at HEAD is GET /get_block?height=N (api_local.rs:2119-2148), which returns the stored block_{h} JSON, and aincore_getFinalityStatus (api_local.rs:903-920), which exposes only last_anchor_round/hash/digest. ChainSync process_blocks (sync/src/lib.rs:928-1010) persists the PEER's block verbatim under block_{h}; reload_chain_tip then calls adopt_synced_anchor with block.committed_vertices verbatim (dag.rs:2852-2884; ordering.rs:869-888), and the local build for that anchor is skipped when anchor_round ≤ latest_block_round (dag.rs:1306-1310). Consequence 1: a node whose local commit path is permanently wedged (hole #1, or any R1 bug) but whose ChainSync works shows blocks identical to the producer's — criterion green while Part I's core mechanism never ran on 3 of 4 nodes. Consequence 2 (the v1 failure the criterion claims to catch): if validator N4's vertices are never cited (hole #2, or any verdict asymmetry), they are in no anchor's cone, so every node — including N4, which commits the same cones locally — produces identical committed_vertices that simply omit N4. 48 h of identical blocks, zero stall, N4 excluded the whole time. The criterion measures cross-node AGREEMENT; silent exclusion is an agreement failure between the DAG and the sequence, which agreement cannot see. Nothing at HEAD records 'built locally' vs 'adopted' per height, and nothing reports per-author citation or inclusion coverage.

§4 says the exit is rows 1–7; §11 Stage 1 says rows 1–8. Row 8 (slashed_author_body_still_admissible_at_its_round) is defined on 'a fetched body' — fetch is §5 (Stage 2–3). In Part I the only way to run it is to call add_vertex directly, which tests the validator_set_at lookup in isolation while the live path's lookup for rounds above the tip is undefined (hole #2). Row 3 (sub_quorum_cited_parents_do_not_propose) asserts 'peers and it converge after redelivery'. In Part I the only redelivery is the below-quorum re-gossip push (dag.rs:881-926); in the row's own fixture the lacking node is 1 of 4, so the three holders stay above quorum and never push, and gossipsub drops a byte-identical re-publish for 60 s anyway (p2p.rs:119-123). The node converges only when ChainSync adopts a block containing the missing vertex (settled without body, dag.rs:2852-2884) — so Part I's liveness after any single loss is secretly dependent on block sync, which the design never states, and the row is satisfiable by the harness handing the vertex to add_vertex regardless of whether the live path could obtain it. Both rows can be green with the live mechanism absent.
fixes: Add to Part I two observable, RPC-exposed signals and put both in the exit criterion: (1) per height, an origin marker (locally_committed | adopted_from_sync) plus the local try_commit decision log (anchor round → commit/skip/defer with the leader hash), and require that every validator's LOCAL decision sequence is identical across nodes and that ≥ X % of heights on every node are locally committed; (2) per round, per author, whether that author's vertex was (a) admitted, (b) Resolved, (c) cited by ≥ 2/3 stake at r+1, (d) present in some block's committed_vertices within k anchors — and require 100 % of honest authors reach (d) for every round of the burn-in. Reject the burn-in if any validator's citation rate at r+1 drops below 2/3 for more than a handful of consecutive rounds.

Make §4 and §11 agree on the row set. Move row 8 to Part II or rewrite it for Part I as 'late-gossip body from a since-removed author, at its own round, arriving after the removing block executed, admitted on a node that executed that block' with the mutation 'use the current set'. Rewrite row 3 so the convergence step is the ONLY mechanism Part I actually has — ChainSync adoption of a block carrying the missing vertex, with gossip fully disabled and no direct add_vertex injection — and state in §12 that Part I's recovery from any single-vertex loss depends on block sync. Add a row whose fixture disables ChainSync and asserts the stall is bounded, or document that it is not.
titles: The Stage 1 burn-in criterion is vacuously satisfiable: ChainSync copies blocks byte-for-byte, no RPC distinguishes a locally built block from an adopted one, and per-validator inclusion is not measured — silent exclusion and a wedged local commit path both pass

Part I's gate is internally inconsistent and two of its rows pass by harness injection of a delivery Part I cannot perform — row 8 needs a fetched body (Part II) and row 3's 'redelivery' does not exist in Part I
Test row 3 asserts convergence 'after redelivery' but Part I has no redelivery; the row is unpassable as specified and the exit criterion cannot observe proposer ejection

claim: A parent that is settled-without-body (committed_set via sync) bypasses the walk's edge check, so the same bytes resolve on one node and not another
sections: 2 (S2), 3 (edge checks and cache rule (b)), 3.3 (R4' 'present parent bodies')
attacks: Section 2 S2 says a settled hash 'may be absent' (committed_set via adopt_synced_anchor, ordering.rs:869-888 through dag.rs:2871-2878, folds the producer's sequence verbatim; the bodies are not delivered). Section 3 says every path must terminate in genesis or committed_set AND every edge child -> parent must satisfy parent.round == child.round - 1 and membership at parent.round. For a parent in committed_set with no body, parent.round and parent.author do not exist. Reading 1 (edge check applied before the settled stop): follower X adopts anchor r whose sequence contains the hash P it lost; X's re-walk of A_{r+1} reaches edge A_{r+1} -> P, cannot read P.round -> invalid -> Unresolved with empty blocked_on; hook (b) fires and fails; X never proposes again after its first adoption - every follower in the design's own burn-in (5% loss forces adoption regularly) is progressively ejected, feeding hole #1. Reading 2 (settled stop before the edge check): a vertex at round 500 may cite a committed round-2 hash and resolve; harmless for I1 but R4' then counts 'present parent bodies' without a round restriction unless specified, and the round-exactness premise that makes 'round-(r-1) candidates' well-defined for rule (c) and R4' is gone. The design does not choose, and the two readings have opposite liveness consequences.

walk_history treats h ∉ dag as settled iff h == 'genesis' or h ∈ committed_set (ordering.rs:697-702) BEFORE any body is inspected; sync adoption puts hashes into committed_set with no body (ordering.rs:869-888 via dag.rs:2852-2884; the design's own S2 'body may be absent'). §3's edge check needs parent.round and parent.author, which come only from the body. Attack: X (leader of even round r) emits V_r with parents = [P, H1_{r-1}, H2_{r-1}] where P is a REAL vertex at round r-5 by author A, already committed everywhere. Node N1 still holds P's body (prune horizon is finalized-10, dag.rs:1786-1808) → edge P has round r-5 ≠ r-1 → V_r Unresolved → not cited. Node N2 lost P in transit (routine 5 % loss, the live row's own parameter) and settled it via sync → walk reaches P ∈ committed_set → settled, edge never evaluated → V_r Resolved → N2 cites it. §3's 'admitted everywhere and resolves nowhere — deterministic' is false, and row 6 (all nodes hold all bodies) cannot observe it. Then R4′: V_r ∈ visited on all nodes (through N2_{r+1}); on N1 present parent bodies = {A, H1, H2} = 3/4 (design does not say wrong-round parents are excluded) → eligible → step 2 commits r at V_r; on N2, P absent → 2/4 → ineligible → defer (hole #1 semantics) → N2's local cursor is stuck at r until it adopts N1's block. Node-local eligibility is exactly the v2 #5 class relocated from ingress to the commit path.
fixes: Specify: a parent hash in committed_set or equal to 'genesis' terminates the path with NO edge check (the committed prefix is the network's decision and needs no re-validation); round-exactness and any membership weighting apply only to edges whose parent body is held. Specify R4' as: distinct-author stake of held parent bodies whose round == anchor.round - 1, over the set used for the anchor decision. Add the test 'adopted_hole_rewalks_and_proposes_again' (ChainSync adoption only, zero add_vertex for the lost hash, node proposes within 2 rounds) with the mutation 'apply the edge check to settled parents'.

Make the settled-without-body case carry what the edge check needs: record (hash, round, author) for every committed vertex (extend Block.committed_vertices / cseq rows, or a parallel committed_meta map bounded with committed_set) so the walk can evaluate round-1 and membership for a bodiless settled parent identically on every node. Define R4′ to count only parents that pass the edge check. Add a row whose fixture has one node with P bodiless-but-settled and whose mutation is 'skip the edge check for committed parents', asserting identical citation and identical anchor eligibility on both nodes.
titles: resolve_walk's edge check is undefined for settled-without-body parents: one reading permanently ejects every node that ever adopted a synced anchor, the other silently drops round-exactness

A parent in committed_set with an absent body bypasses the edge check, so the same bytes resolve on one node and not another; R4′'s 'present parent bodies' count then diverges and one side commits while the other defers

claim: E2 is neither total nor intersection-sound: the middle band is undecidable, a skip can coexist with another node's direct commit, and untwinned vs twin-aware nodes apply different rules
sections: §3.1 R4 ('cites only resolved round-(r−1) vertices') read with §6 ('resolve_walk reads dag
§6 E2 bullet 2 ('If the walked round-(r+1) set held ≥ 2/3 stake and Σ votes ≤ 1/3: skip …
§6 E2 bullet 3 ('Otherwise defer and WANTED the missing round-(r+1) votes') together with
§6 E2 bullet 4 ('Step 2 never decides a twinned round by visited … For an untwinned leader
§6 Rule E2 ('If the walked round-(r+1) set held >= 2/3 stake and sum_t votes(t) <= 1/3: sk
§6 Rule E2 ('Otherwise defer and WANTED the missing round-(r+1) votes'); §10 row `leader_e
§6 Rule E2 (skip branch); §7 row 2; §10 rows `leader_equivocation_A3_B1` / `_A2_B2`
§6 Rule E2 (three bullets), §7 row 2, §10 rows `leader_equivocation_A3_B1` / `_A2_B2`.
attacks: n=4 equal stake, honest H1,H2,H3, Byzantine X = leader(r). X builds twins A,B at r. X delivers A to H1 early; delays A to H2 and H3 until after each has proposed its r+1 vertex (H2,H3 cite {H1_r,H2_r,H3_r} = 3/4 > 2/3, so R4 lets them propose without any twin); then X sends A followed by B to H3 only (direct TCP, `send_message`). State: H1 holds A (dag) and cited A at r+1; H2 holds A only; H3 holds A (dag) + B (shadow, S4). Round-(r+1) votes everywhere: H1→A, H2→∅, H3→∅, X→∅ or absent. Round r+2 leader is honest and its vertex cites {H1_{r+1},H2_{r+1},H3_{r+1}}; r+3 votes give it a direct commit. Step 2 now decides r on each node: H1 and H2 have `leader_vertex_hash(r) = {A}` (untwinned) so, per §6 last bullet 'for an untwinned leader, step 2 is unchanged', they use `visited`: H1_{r+1} ∈ visited and it cites A, so A ∈ visited → COMMIT r at A (ordering.rs:583-597). H3 has twins {A,B} so it must use E2: walked r+1 set = 4/4 ≥ 2/3, Σ votes = 1/4 ≤ 1/3 → SKIP r. H1/H2 build height h from anchor A (round r); H3 builds height h from round r+2 — the B4b block fork. Nothing ever repairs it: nobody cites B, so H1/H2 never WANTED it; EQUIV_PROOF gossip from H3 cannot create a shadow on H1/H2 because §10 `phantom_proof_does_not_change_anchors` requires proofs not to change decisions (and if proofs DID create shadows, that test fails instead — the design is caught both ways). The same fork also occurs with no delivery trick at all whenever one node decides r before the second twin reaches it and another decides after. This is exactly the v2 root-cause class: §6 claims the decision 'never depends on which twin arrived first' but it depends on WHETHER a twin has arrived at decision time. The consistency argument in §6 ('a node that already committed r directly at t … every node that later learns of the twin still reaches commit at t') covers only DIRECT commits; it says nothing about the far more common ancestry commit, and that is where it breaks.

n=4 equal stake, X = leader(r) sends A to H1,H2 and B to H3 (each first), then the counterpart to everyone, so every honest node holds both twins (dag + shadow). Round-(r+1) votes: H1→A, H2→A, H3→B, X→∅ (X cites only {H1_r,H2_r,H3_r}, which is a legal 3/4 parent set) or X sends nothing. Every honest node holds all four r+1 bodies. E2 on every node: votes(A)=2/4 (not > 2/3), votes(B)=1/4, Σ=3/4 > 1/3 → neither commit nor skip → 'defer and WANTED the missing round-(r+1) votes' — but no vote is missing; every author's r+1 body is held. Step 1 scans past r to a later direct anchor r_direct; step 2 reaches j=r and, per §6, may not decide it by `visited`, so it returns `out` empty (ordering.rs:583-597 pattern); the cursor never advances (only apply_anchor_bookkeeping advances it, ordering.rs:776). No node ever produces a block ≥ r, so ChainSync/adopt_synced_anchor (dag.rs:2852-2884) has nothing to adopt. Total, permanent liveness failure from a single validator key, cheaper than HEAD's wedge (no fake parent needed). At n=7 the same holds with a 3:2 honest split and X,Y silent at r+1 (max twin votes 3/7 < 5/7 required, Σ=5/7 > 1/3). Bullshark closes this band by ancestry from the next anchor; v3 removed that path for twinned rounds and supplied no replacement.
fixes: There must be ONE decision function for every leader round, evaluated identically whether or not the node knows of a twin. Adopt Mysticeti's uncertified-DAG rule (research A: 'support' rule) in place of E2 + the untwinned/twinned split: (1) each round-(r+1) vertex SUPPORTS exactly one vertex per (author, round) — the first twin reached in a deterministic order over its parent list — so a vertex citing both twins still supports one; (2) DIRECT commit of t requires a certificate pattern visible in the cone: > 2/3 stake of round-(r+2) vertices each of whose parents include > 2/3 stake of round-(r+1) supporters of t; (3) DIRECT skip requires > 2/3 stake of round-(r+1) vertices that do not support t (blame); (4) otherwise decide INDIRECTLY from the lowest later committed anchor: commit t iff that anchor's cone contains a certificate for t, else skip. Because certificates and blames are cone-visible, a node that never sees the twin and a node that holds both evaluate the same predicate on the same cone. Delete the sentence 'for an untwinned leader, step 2 is unchanged' and re-run the §10 A3_B1/A2_B2 tests with the twin delivered to ONE node only and to NO node until after one node has decided r.

A leader round must always be decidable once the next anchor is committed: replace defer-forever with the indirect rule from hole 1 (decide r from the lowest later committed anchor's cone — commit t iff the cone certifies t, else skip). Deferral is only permitted while the cone is INCOMPLETE (a genuine hole), never while it is complete. Add a test `twinned_round_split_2_1_offender_silent_is_decided_within_two_anchors` whose mutation is 'keep E2's defer branch'.
titles: Decision rule is selected by local twin knowledge: untwinned nodes decide r by ancestry, twin-aware nodes by E2, and the two rules disagree
E2's middle band (1/3 < Σ votes, no twin > 2/3) is undecidable with complete information: one equivocating leader halts the chain forever
E2's skip rule is not intersection-sound: a > 2/3 direct commit and a '≥ 2/3 walked, ≤ 1/3 Σ' skip coexist when the offender also twins its r+1 vote
E2 skip rule is not quorum-intersection-sound: one node commits round r at twin t while another skips r

E2 is not total: a leader-equivocation split with no twin > 2/3 and Σ > 1/3 while every round-(r+1) body is held is a permanent defer — chain halt with one Byzantine leader who withholds its own r+1 vote
E2 skip rule is unsound: a node can skip round r while another already committed it directly (v3's own 'arrival order irrelevant' claim is false)
E2 has no terminal decision when all r+1 votes are held and split: one equivocation permanently halts the chain (and test A2_B2 asserts an outcome E2 never produces)
'At most one twin can pass' silently assumes every honest r+1 vertex cites at most one twin, but §3.1 + §6 let the proposer's candidate list include the shadow

claim: The compact shadow has no payload, so a committed cone containing the second twin yields different block content on nodes holding it live vs as shadow; it is also not self-authenticating through the ingress gate
sections: §5.3 'vertex:{H} or vertex_shadow:{H}'; §6 'Shadow storage'; dag.rs:1036-1042, 1062-1070;
§6 'Shadow storage' ('compact form plus parents'), §5.3 ('vertex:{H} or vertex_shadow:{H}
§6 'Shadow storage' (compact + parents) and 'No exclusion rule is needed'; §2 S4; dag.rs:1
§6 'Shadow storage' (compact form plus parents; 'the walk needs parents, not payload') and
§6 Shadow storage ('compact form plus parents — the walk needs parents, not payload'); §6
attacks: n=4. X = leader(r) sends A first to H1,H2 and B first to H3; the counterpart follows. H3 holds B in dag/round_index and A in shadow (compact + parents, no payload). Votes: H1→A, H2→A, H3→B, X→A (X's single r+1 vertex). votes(A)=3/4 → E2 commits r at A on EVERY node (this is the design's happy path, §7 row 2). On H3, `commit_one_anchor(A)`: `find_causal_history` (ordering.rs:964-1010) does `dag.get(&hash)` at :975 — A is not in `dag`, so A itself is not pushed into `history` and its parents are not traversed (a parent P cited only by A is silently omitted); the sort at :1002 puts any hash not in `dag` last. So H3's committed sequence (a) omits A's exclusive ancestry, (b) orders A's cone differently from H1/H2, and the finality digest diverges. Even if find_causal_history is changed to read dag ∪ shadow, the block-build loop (dag.rs:1345-1383) does `dag.get(hash)` per sequence hash: for A it hits the else-branch, prints COMMIT_VERTEX_MISSING and drops A's transactions from `block_txs` — and the shadow has no payload to supply anyway (compact form strips it, blockchain/src/lib.rs:454-461). H1/H2 execute A's transactions; H3 does not → different state root, different block hash at the same height. Symmetrically, when both twins are in the cone (H3's r+1 vertex cites B), H1/H2 lack B's payload and H3 lacks A's: every node executes a different transaction set for height h. §6 'the sequence orders whatever the cone contains' is therefore a fork, not a determinism argument. Note the shadow is arrival-defined ('the first counterpart'): which twin is compact is exactly the arrival-order dependence v3 set out to remove.

Non-leader Z at round r sends V (payload P1) to N1,N2 and V' (payload P2) to N3,N4. Each side cites its own twin at r+1 (both resolve locally). The anchor at r+2 cites both r+1 sides, so its cone contains V and V'. Per §5/§6 every node fetches the other twin and stores it as 'compact form plus parents' (§6: 'the walk needs parents, not payload'). §6 then says 'the sequence orders whatever the cone contains' (no exclusion rule). At block-build time dag.rs:1345-1385 reads `dag.get(hash)` for each hash in commit.sequence and pushes `v.payload` into block_txs; a shadow is 'never in round_index' and not in `dag`, so on N1 the loop either omits V' entirely (find_causal_history at ordering.rs:964-975 only pushes hashes with `dag.get(&hash).is_some()`, so V' is not even in N1's sequence, while it is in N3's) or hits the [COMMIT_VERTEX_MISSING] branch whose own comment says 'block content will diverge'. N1 executes P1 only, N3 executes P2 only (and V' contributes a BFT-time sample on N3 but not N1, dag.rs:1375). Different committed_vertices, different txs, different state root, different block hash at the same height: fork with f=1. v2's exclusion rule was dropped because it was keyed on local state; v3 dropped the rule but kept the payload-less shadow, so the sequence is still node-local.
fixes: Any vertex that can be an anchor or appear in a committed sequence must be held in LIVE form with payload on every node, and every consumer must read one store. Simplest sound option (research C:121 option (a)): admit BOTH twins into `dag`/`round_index` as live vertices (they are hash-bound and signed), drop the shadow tier entirely, keep the slash via evidence, and bound per-author bytes per round window (I4/I11) instead of per-(author, round) count. If a shadow tier is kept, it must store the full live body and `walk_history`, `find_causal_history`, the sort key, and dag.rs:1346 must all read dag ∪ shadow, with an explicit test `winning_twin_held_as_shadow_executes_same_block` (mutation: 'store shadow compact').

Either (a) store the shadow as the FULL live body (payload included; it is bounded by MAX_VERTEX_BYTES and there is at most one per (author, round)) and make find_causal_history, the block builder's payload loop, and BFT-time sampling read dag ∪ shadow; or (b) keep compact shadows and add a deterministic exclusion keyed only on DAG-carried facts: a twin is excluded from the executed payload iff the other twin is also in the cone (both nodes then see the same pair and both drop both payloads while keeping the hashes in committed_vertices). Test: `equivocating_nonleader_in_cone_identical_block_hash` with 3:1 and 2:2 splits, asserting byte-identical block_txs and state root; mutation: strip payload from shadow.

Compact shadow twin has no payload and is invisible to find_causal_history and the block builder: any committed cone containing the second twin forks the sequence or the executed transactions

claim: One shadow per (author, round) recreates I9 for a third twin and makes the twin set arrival-ordered again
sections: §6 'Shadow storage' ('at most one shadow per (author, round) — the first counterpart … any
§6 'Shadow storage' (at most one shadow per (author, round); further bodies dropped withou
§6 'Shadow storage': 'at most one shadow per (author, round) — the first counterpart'; §7
§6 Shadow storage ('at most one shadow per (author, round) — the first counterpart; any fu
attacks: n=4. X = leader(r) or not (irrelevant). X signs three same-round vertices A, B, C. It delivers A first to H1, B first to H2, C first to H3, then all remaining versions to everyone. Under §6 each node keeps its first-arrived twin in dag and exactly ONE counterpart as shadow ('the first counterpart … any further same-round body from that author is dropped without writing', the `sys:equiv_seen` latch dag.rs:2287-2290): H1 holds {A,B}, drops C; H2 holds {B,C}, drops A; H3 holds {C,A}, drops B (X orders deliveries to make this so). Each honest node cites its own dag twin at r+1 (round_index). The honest leader of r+2 cites {H1,H2,H3}_{r+1} (3/4 > 2/3), so the anchor cone at r+2 contains A, B and C. On every node, `walk_history` (ordering.rs:697-712, or resolve_walk over dag ∪ shadow) hits the version it dropped → hole → `commit_one_anchor` returns None (ordering.rs:731-737). WANTED fires for the missing hash, the fetch reaches a peer that holds it, `VERTEX_RESP` delivers it, and the ingress latch drops it again without writing. No node ever commits r+2 or anything above; no block exists for adopt_synced_anchor to heal from. This is exactly the audit-119 I9 wedge, now requiring three signatures instead of two, and it is a direct consequence of the I4 bound chosen in §6.

n=4 {H1,H2,H3,Z}. Z signs three vertices V1,V2,V3 at round r and delivers exactly one to each honest node (V_i -> H_i), then produces nothing at r+1. Each H_i resolves and cites V_i at r+1 (plus the honest round-r vertices; 4/4 stake, R4 satisfied). At r+2 every H_i walks the other two r+1 vertices: H_j's cites V_j -> WANTED[V_j] -> fetched from H_j -> ingress: (Z, r) already has dag twin V_i; §6 stores 'at most one shadow per (author, round) — the first counterpart' and 'any further same-round body from that author is dropped without writing (the existing sys:equiv_seen latch, dag.rs:2287-2290)'. So H_i can store V_j but V_k is dropped forever; H_k's r+1 vertex is Unresolved on H_i forever. Citable r+1 stake on every honest node = 2/4 = 50% <= 2/3 -> R4 fails -> no honest node ever proposes r+2. The tick re-walk re-fetches V_k every tick and the latch drops it every tick. No new vertex means no evidence carrier (drain_evidence_for_vertex runs only inside a successful try_create_vertex, dag.rs:648), so the slash never lands and Z is never removed; even if it were, 2/3 of the remaining 3 is not > 2/3. Same arithmetic for any n: three groups of (n-1)/3, any node resolves two of them = 2(n-1)/3 < 2n/3. Cost to Z: three signatures.
fixes: The bound must be on what honest nodes can CITE, not on count: an honest round-(r+1) vertex cites at most one twin, so at most n distinct twins can ever be in any cone. Bound held versions per (author, round) by the validator count (or, better, admit all hash-distinct twins into `dag` and bound by bytes per author per window per I4/I11 — a few hundred bytes each if payload-stripped is acceptable for non-anchors, full body otherwise per hole 4). Add test `three_way_equivocation_does_not_wedge` (mutation: 'cap shadows at 1').

Bound shadows per (author, round) by the number of DISTINCT twins actually cited by held vertices (each additional twin costs the attacker one honest citer, so the bound is <= number of validators), not by a constant 1; store any twin that some held round-(r+1) body cites. Alternatively make R1 treat 'cites a twin of a known equivocator at (author, round)' as resolved once ANY twin is held (the cone then contains whichever twins are held, which is why fix #2 must be applied first). Test `three_way_equivocation_does_not_halt`: n=4, three twins split 1:1:1, assert every honest node proposes r+2 and identical anchors; mutation: cap shadows at 1.

claim: Fetch cannot bridge a gap deeper than the serving peer's prune margin (~10 rounds below finality), so the I10 rejoin claim is false
sections: §5.3 server (`vertex:{H}` or `vertex_shadow:{H}`), §5.4 exclusion/TTL and 'Exit on … `roun
§5.4 exit conditions; §5.5 release timing; §9 row I10 'boot walk + fetch'; §10 row `restar
§9 I10 row ('boot walk (bounded ≤ current+2) + fetch'); §10 row `restart_rejoin_without_ch
attacks: Progressing validators call prune_dag(min(finalized, latest_block_round) − 10) every 10 blocks (dag.rs:1786-1808, 2770-2783), deleting both `dag` entries and `vertex:{H}` rows. A validator that restarts after G > 10 rounds (30 s at the 3 s tick; the catalogued I10 case is 30-60 rounds) comes back with committed_set at its old cursor. Test row `restart_rejoin_without_chainsync` disables ChainSync, so committed_set never moves. Every round-(current−1) candidate's resolve_walk (floor 0, §3) descends through the band [old cursor, current) ; every hash below every peer's horizon is answered `unknown` by all holders, excluded until TTL, and never fills. R4 is therefore never met, the node never proposes, and its own try_commit cannot advance because the lowest anchor's cone is in the pruned band — exactly the wedge I10 describes, now made permanent by Part I's R4 instead of by parent_quorum. Even inside the retention window the design descends one level per tick (§5.5: 'invalidate … re-walk those on the next tick'; §5.1: the trigger is the once-per-tick proposer walk), so a 10-round band costs ≥ 10 ticks during which 10 new rounds arrive; with ChainSync on this converges only because sync adoption moves the floor, i.e. I10 is carried by HEAD's ChainSync path, not by Part II. Finally §5.4's exit 'round < prune_horizon' refers to the absent body's round, which §5.2 itself says is unobservable ('defined on what the node can observe … not on the absent body's fields'); as written the exit never fires and the entry lives to TTL.

Serving reads `vertex:{H}` (§5.3), and `prune_dag` deletes that row and the in-memory entry on every node for `round < min(finalized_round, latest_block_round) − 10` every 10 blocks (dag.rs:1786-1808, :2770-2783, `storage.delete` at :2779). Sequence per §10 row 15: 4 validators, N4 down 30 rounds with ChainSync 'fully disabled'. N4 restarts with `committed_set` at ≈ round R (its own last commits). Live vertices at R+30 arrive; after a quorum is held `current_round` = R+31 (dag.rs:1231-1240). Proposer walk from R+30 candidates descends the held band and blocks on all of R+29 → Tier A WANTED → fetched (peers hold ≥ F−10 ≈ R+18) → admitted → re-walk → R+28 … → R+18 fetched; R+17 and below: every peer answers `unknown` (rows deleted) → each peer excluded for that hash until TTL (§5.4) → entry expires at 64 ticks → recreated by the next tick's walk → infinite unknown loop. Because the walk is floor-0 and terminates only at `committed_set ∪ genesis` (§3), and committed_set cannot advance without either a local commit (impossible: try_commit's own walk_history has the same hole, ordering.rs:697-702) or sync adoption (disabled), N4 never resolves any round-(current−1) candidate → R4 fails forever → N4 never proposes again. The same happens with ChainSync ON whenever it cannot deliver: `gather_and_check_seed_tips` disagreement returns before any block (sync :607-622), all peers session-only (:626-632), or the peer has pruned below the node's height (:736-747, 'bootstrap from a state snapshot'). A 3:1 partition healed after > 10 rounds puts the minority node in exactly this state.
fixes: State the fetch window explicitly: vertex fetch heals holes with citer.round − 1 ≥ (network finalized − 10); anything deeper is healed only by ChainSync adoption (settled-without-body), which must therefore remain mandatory and the test row must be rewritten as 'gap ≤ retention window' or dropped. Compute the exit as `citer.round − 1 < prune_horizon` (observable). Add a VERTEX_RESP `below_horizon` per-hash signal (mirroring SyncResponse.prune_horizon) so the requester stops asking and triggers block sync immediately. Re-walk on admission inside the fetcher (bounded to the released dependents) rather than on the next tick, so a k-level band resolves in k fetch RTTs, not k ticks. Test: restart with G = 40 rounds, ChainSync ON, assert the node proposes within 20 ticks; mutation: exit on unobservable round.

State the dependency honestly: Part II fetch recovers only the uncommitted cone; anything below a serving peer's `min_round` must be SETTLED, not obtained. Add a `VERTEX_RESP.settled: [(hash, height)]` answer for pruned hashes (the server can map hash → block via `consensus:cseq:{round}` / block.committed_vertices while those rows exist, or a small hash→height index kept for the prune window), and on receipt the requester runs the existing QC-verified block adoption for that height (ChainSync's `apply_finality_artifact` + `adopt_synced_anchor`) — i.e. fetch-below-horizon forces the settlement path immediately instead of looping on `unknown`. Make `unknown` from > 1/3 stake for a hash trigger an immediate `sync_from_peers` rather than a 64-tick TTL. Rewrite row 15 to 'ChainSync serving only (no gossip), gap > cone' and add a row 'minority partition 3:1 healed after 40 rounds, all four converge'.
titles: I10 rejoin claim is false: peers prune below finalized−10, so any gap > ~10 rounds is unfetchable, and the 'round < prune_horizon' exit is computed on a field the fetcher cannot observe

Fetch can never bridge a gap deeper than the serving peer's prune margin (~10 rounds below its finality): the `restart_rejoin_without_chainsync` row is unpassable and a minority partition > 10 rounds wedges without ChainSync

claim: All Part II timers are in receiver ticks, but the tick is an operator knob with a 100 ms floor, so the 2-tick deadline starves honest fetches on a real WAN
sections: §5.4 'Per-request deadline: 2 receiver ticks'; §5.2 'TTL of 64 ticks', 'one frame per 16 t
attacks: Tick = AINCORE_CONSENSUS_TICK_MS, default 3000, floor 100 (main.rs:633-637); the burn-in ran at 500 ms (dag.rs:766-777 records exactly this class of bug: 'a liveness knob must not silently change meaning when a performance knob is turned'). One fetch = TCP connect (1 RTT) + client ephemeral -> server hello (1 RTT) + HELLO -> WELCOME (1 RTT) + VERTEX_REQ -> VERTEX_RESP (1 RTT) (network/src/lib.rs:426-540, 207-233) = 4 RTT = 600 ms on the design's 150 ms WAN, plus two Ed25519 sign/verify, plus up to 1 MiB of reply on a Pi uplink (20 Mbit/s ≈ 420 ms). At 500 ms tick the 2-tick deadline is 1.0 s: a full-size honest response (one 768 KiB vertex) misses it; the holder is excluded until TTL (64 ticks = 32 s); the second witness is tried and excluded; the entry dies. At the 100 ms floor the deadline (200 ms) is below one RTT chain, so no WAN fetch ever completes, TTL is 6.4 s, and Tier B's 'one frame per 16 ticks' is 1.6 s. No attacker is needed; the stall is worst for the largest (fullest) vertices, i.e. under load. Conversely at a 3 s tick the deadline (6 s) exceeds the 5 s connect timeout but is far below the transport's 120 s frame timeouts, so the abort must actively cancel the task or the socket and pool slot leak for up to 120 s.
fixes: Define fetch timers in wall time with a floor independent of the tick: deadline = max(2 ticks, 5 s) (or 4 × measured RTT to that peer + size/bandwidth estimate), TTL = max(64 ticks, 180 s), Tier B frame interval = max(16 ticks, 30 s); document that the tick is a proposal cadence, not a network RTT. Cancel the socket on deadline (tokio::time::timeout around the whole connect+request future) so pool slots are released. Test `fetch_deadline_at_100ms_tick_over_150ms_link` with a delayed-socket harness; mutation: deadline in ticks only.
titles: All Part II timers are in receiver ticks, but the tick is an operator knob (100 ms floor) and one fetch needs 4 WAN round trips plus a 1 MiB body

claim: The VERTEX_REQ server has no per-peer byte or CPU budget: one unauthenticated connection amplifies ~450x and saturates a Raspberry Pi validator
sections: §5.3 Messages; §7 'VERTEX_REQ flood'; §9 I15; network/src/lib.rs:207-233, 239; sync/src/li
attacks: Any TCP client that completes the X25519 exchange may send requests (research B: `__`-prefixed ids are accepted; no validator key needed). Per connection the transport allows 100 msg/s (network/src/lib.rs:207-233); the design allows 32 hashes per request and a reply up to 1 MiB (§5.3), served from storage with no consensus lock. Attacker sends VERTEX_REQ for 32 real 768 KiB hashes (learned from gossip) at 100 req/s: server does up to 64 RocksDB gets, JSON-serialises up to 32 × 768 KiB = 24 MiB per request unless it trims incrementally (the design does not say; nothing forbids the same hash 32 times), then ChaCha20-Poly1305-encrypts (crypto/transport.rs:1-2) and writes 1 MiB. Per connection: 100 MiB/s ≈ 840 Mbit/s egress and ≈ 100 MiB/s AEAD + serde. A Cortex-A72 core does ~150-250 MB/s ChaCha20-Poly1305 and comparable serde throughput, so one connection pins ≥ 1 core and the NIC; four connections from ONE IP (cap 60) pin all four cores. Request bytes ≈ 2.3 KB -> reply 1 MiB: ≈ 450× amplification, paid by the victim's uplink, so its own DAG_VERTEX broadcasts, QC votes, and honest VERTEX_RESPs to peers are starved. The ticker (`consensus.write()` every tick) and the gossip consumer share those cores. §7 dismisses 'VERTEX_REQ flood' with '§5 quotas', but every §5 quota is requester-side; §9 marks I15 'server cost bounded'. (SYNC_REQ at sync/src/lib.rs:1213-1218 has the same shape today — 500 blocks, no byte cap — so this is not a new class, but Part II adds a second, hash-addressable instance and claims the bound.)
fixes: Server-side: reject requests with duplicate hashes; cap hashes per request at 8 and serve at most one MAX_VERTEX_BYTES body per reply beyond the first (trim while serialising, never build then trim); a per-connection byte budget (e.g. 4 MiB per 10 s) and a per-IP request budget (e.g. 20 req/s) enforced in the handler; prefer serving from a small LRU of pre-serialised `vertex:{H}` strings so a hot hash costs no serde; unauthenticated sessions get a lower budget than sessions whose HELLO authenticates as a validator. State the Pi numbers in §12. Test `vertex_req_flood_keeps_tick_under_100ms`: 4 attacker connections at 100 req/s, assert ticker latency and honest fetch completion; mutation: remove the byte budget.
titles: VERTEX_REQ server has no per-peer byte or CPU budget: ~450x amplification saturates a Raspberry Pi validator from one unauthenticated connection

claim: Exclude-on-timeout until TTL, combined with the unreserved 100-slot TCP accept cap, lets two IPs stop every honest fetch
sections: §5.2 Tier B ('request it from X only'), §5.4 ('Exclude for that hash, until TTL, any peer
§5.4 'Exclude for that hash, until TTL, any peer that timed out…'; §9 I15 'TCP slots = Sta
attacks: Unauthenticated attacker opens 60 sessions from IP-a and 40 from IP-b to each validator (network/src/lib.rs:108-131: MAX_CONNECTIONS=100 checked before the per-IP cap of 60), sends the 32-byte ephemeral key so the handshake completes, then idles; the server's frame-length read times out after 60 s (lib.rs:211-215) so the attacker reconnects every 59 s (or holds the 10 s handshake window, lib.rs:159-166). Every honest `secure_connect` to that validator is accepted by the kernel and immediately dropped by the `continue` at lib.rs:108-113 -> EOF/timeout inside the 2-tick deadline. §5.4 then excludes that peer 'for that hash, until TTL' (64 ticks = 192 s at the 3 s tick); the next attempt hits the next witness, also starved; within 2-3 attempts every witness and every 'validator with peer_ip' is excluded and the WANTED entry idles to TTL, is evicted, is re-inserted by the tick re-walk, and repeats. Meanwhile Part I's R4 stops any node that cannot resolve > 2/3 of round-(r-1) from proposing, and ordinary 5 % loss (design §1) produces a hole on some validator every few rounds. Result: chain-wide proposal stop for as long as ~200 idle sockets are held, at ~zero bandwidth, with no validator key. Stage 3 ships before Stage 5 (§11), so this window is real; and even after slot reservation the exclusion rule converts every transient failure (Pi under load, NAT reset) into a 64-tick blacklist. If the fetcher classifies the EOF as an error rather than a timeout, backoff min(2^k,16) ticks gives the same outcome with a 16-tick recovery lag.

Honest X's vertex X_r is lost at every receiver (the row's own scenario). X_{r+1} cites it → Tier B WANTED[X_r] with X as the only permitted peer. Attacker (no key needed) fills X's 100 inbound TCP sessions (network/src/lib.rs:108, I15 open at HEAD, 'Stage 5' per §9), or X is simply slow: the single request misses the 2-tick deadline → X excluded for that hash until TTL → no other peer allowed → entry idles to 64 ticks, is deleted, and is re-created fresh by the next tick re-walk → next attempt. Effective rate: one attempt per ~64 ticks. Throughout, X_r and every X vertex above it are unresolvable everywhere, X's r+1.. vertices are never cited (R4), X's leader rounds are skipped by proof (no votes), and X earns no rewards — an unauthenticated peer excludes a validator from consensus for as long as it holds the slots. Row `self_vertex_lost_everywhere_fetched_from_author` runs in a lab without slot exhaustion and cannot fail on this.
fixes: Never exclude a peer on timeout or connect failure — exclude only on an explicit `unknown` or an invalid body, and even then for a short bounded window (e.g. 4 ticks), with per-peer backoff instead of per-hash exclusion. Make Stage 5 (validator-reserved accept slots: reserve n slots for sessions whose HELLO authenticates as a current validator, evict the oldest unauthenticated session when full) a prerequisite of Stage 3, not a follow-up. Test `slot_exhaustion_does_not_blacklist_holders`: fill the target's accept cap from two IPs, assert Tier A fetch completes within the TTL once one slot frees; mutation: exclude on timeout.

Tier B may target the author first but must fall back to any peer that has since admitted the body (peers that witnessed it become Tier A holders once they admit it), and the per-hash exclusion must not apply to the sole permitted peer; alternatively, make Stage 5 (I15 slot reservation) a prerequisite of Stage 3 rather than a follow-on. Test: X's inbound sessions saturated by a non-validator; assert X_r is still admitted within the TTL.
titles: Exclude-on-timeout until TTL, combined with the unreserved 100-slot TCP accept cap, lets two IPs stop every honest fetch and therefore every honest proposal
Tier B is single-shot: 'author only' plus 'exclude on timeout until TTL' gives one 2-tick attempt per 64 ticks, and an unauthenticated peer can force the timeout (I15 not done)

claim: Tier B 'from the author only' is unreachable for an author with no routable peer_ip
sections: §5.2 Tier B (request it from X only), §5.4 'Whom: witnesses first…, then validators with `
attacks: n=4; validator X is behind NAT and dials OUT to N1..N3 (the documented multi-machine topology). N1..N3 hold only inbound sessions from X, so `storage.get_peer_ip(X)` is None on all of them — exactly the case sync/src/lib.rs:626-632 skips because 'their accepted socket source is not a routable sync target'. X's round-r vertex X_r is broadcast once (dag.rs:1884) and lost at all three (gossipsub mesh flap; the memory notes this exact one-shot loss bootstrapped a live deadlock). X is above quorum so it never re-gossips (:881 branch only fires below quorum). X_{r+1} cites X_r (X holds it). On N1: resolve_walk(X_{r+1}) → blocked on X_r; witnesses = {X} = 25% ≤ 1/3 → Tier B → request X only → `secure_connect(peer_ip(X)…)` has no address → cannot request; Tier A never applies because nobody but X will ever cite X_{r+1} (Part I: honest nodes cite only resolved vertices). Every subsequent X_{r+k} chains through X_{r+1} → X_r, so with the floor-0 walk EVERY future X vertex is Unresolved on N1..N3 forever. Consequences: X's stake is never cited (R4 on honest nodes runs on 75% — one more loss of any kind and R4 fails everywhere → halt); every even round X leads is skipped (§3.4: cited by no honest vertex → not in visited); X_r never enters any anchor cone so it never settles via commit or sync (committed_vertices come from cones), so the condition is permanent; X itself sees nothing wrong (its own walk resolves its chain) and keeps proposing into the void. Two NAT'd validators in this state at n=4 → cited stake ≤ 50% → chain halt with zero Byzantine actors.
fixes: Add the missing holder-side push, which I2 permits: a proposer that observes its own round-r vertex is cited by NO held round-(r+1) body from > 1/3 stake (observable from held bodies, O(n)) re-broadcasts that vertex once per 16 ticks (bounded, own-tick scheduled, idempotent at ingress by hash dedup at dag.rs:1143). Make Tier B fall back to 'any peer with a live session' (the inbound session itself is a valid reply channel — the request can be answered over the existing encrypted socket the author opened) rather than requiring `peer_ip`; and have the author advertise a routable address in its vertex or handshake so `peer_ip` exists for inbound-only peers. Test: X with no `peer_ip` on any peer, X_r dropped at all receivers, assert X_r admitted everywhere within 32 ticks and X's leader rounds not skipped; mutation = 'remove holder re-broadcast'.
titles: Tier B 'from the author only' is unreachable for an author without a routable `peer_ip`; a self-vertex lost everywhere then makes every later vertex of that author unresolvable on every node, permanently — zombie validator, and a second one halts the chain

claim: Boot loops set current_round from the max replayed vertex round, so one far-future vertex plus a routine restart silences the fetch trigger
sections: §5.1 trigger (proposer walk only), §5.2 '(far-future admitted vertices are the I11 bound,
attacks: Attacker validator sends ONE vertex V with round = current_round + 9_999 (passes the jump guard dag.rs:963 `≤ current + MAX_ROUND_JUMP`, PWN-003 future-timestamp check, signature, non-empty parents, membership). It is persisted at `vertex:{H}` (dag.rs:1170) and gossiped to every node. Ingress fast-forward is quorum-gated (:1231-1240) so nothing happens live. Then any node restarts (rolling deploy, the memory notes one reboot froze the chain for 10 days). All three boot loops do `if vertex.round > max_round { max_round = vertex.round }` unconditionally (dag.rs:224, :271, :337) and `final_start_round = max(1, max_round + 1)` (:430-437) → current_round = current+10_000. `try_create_vertex` (:529-536) takes `round_index[current−1]` = [V] only; parent_quorum_met false → below-quorum branch (:881) forever. Part II's only trigger is 'the proposer's own resolve_walk' over round-(current−1) candidates (§5.1, §3 (c)): the sole candidate is V, whose walk blocks on V's fake parents → WANTED with witness = attacker → Tier B → attacker answers `unknown` → TTL. Nothing else is ever WANTed because there are no other candidates at that round. `add_vertex` fast-forward (:1231) and `reload_chain_tip` (:3001 `if next_round > self.current_round`) only ever RAISE current_round; live vertices at the real round are admitted but are 10_000 rounds below the proposal clock. The node commits (cursor-driven) but never proposes; at 3 s ticks that is ≥ 8 hours of exclusion per restart. Every node received V, so a rolling restart of validators holding > 1/3 stake halts the chain (R4 on the remaining nodes cannot reach > 2/3 cited stake). The comment at dag.rs:2937-2946 already records that closing one door (ingress) then a second (reload) was 'not enough'; the boot loop is the third door and it is wide open.
fixes: Derive the boot round the same way ingress and reload do: after replay, `current_round = max(quorum_round(round_idx, dag, validators) + 1, latest_proposed_round + 1)` — never `max_round + 1` — with `latest_proposed_round` itself only ever written from quorum-gated paths (it already is: :1237, :3006). Additionally clamp replayed far-future vertices at boot: do not index a vertex with `round > quorum_round + MAX_ROUND_JUMP/2` into `round_index` (keep it in storage, or drop it — it can never become a parent). Add a Part II trigger that does not depend on the proposal clock: also walk round-(quorum_round) candidates, so a wrong `current_round` cannot starve WANTED. Test: one far-future vertex, restart, assert the node proposes within 4 ticks and WANTED is populated from the live round; mutation = 'boot from max_round'.
titles: Boot loops set current_round from the maximum replayed vertex round; one admitted far-future vertex plus a routine restart silences the Part II trigger — the restarted validator never walks, never WANTs, never proposes until the network reaches that round

claim: The trigger is proposer-only, so observers, jailed validators and partitioned nodes never populate WANTED and never fetch
sections: §5.1 ('The trigger is the proposer's own resolve_walk'; secondary trigger 'walk_history's
attacks: At HEAD, `try_create_vertex` returns for a non-validator at dag.rs:607-612 (RULE 1) before the below-quorum branch, so the R4 evaluation and the §3 rule-(c) tick re-walk — Part II's primary WANTED source — never run on an observer (indexer, RPC, DEX, or a jailed validator, which is an observer until unjailed). The secondary trigger lives in try_commit, which is invoked only from add_vertex (dag.rs:1290) and is skipped outright on observers (:1242-1251). Sequence: indexer node loses one gossip vertex → its DAG has a permanent hole → no WANTED entry is ever created → local ordering (if enabled) defers forever; it serves state only via ChainSync adoption, which is the exact I6 failure ('orphans never drained on indexer/RPC/DEX/jailed nodes') with 'orphans' renamed 'holes'. Jailed validator: unjailed after N rounds, its DAG has N rounds of holes it never fetched → the hole-5 I10 loop begins from a worse position. Validators: E2's 'defer and WANTED the missing round-(r+1) votes' executes inside try_commit, which only runs when a vertex arrives; a node that is the last one waiting (everyone else deferring on it, or a partition heal with no new vertices) never re-runs the decision — I14's 'the event that should trigger recovery is the event the failure suppressed'.
fixes: Drive WANTED population and try_commit from the node's own tick for every node role (observer included): a tick-scheduled `resolve_walk` over round_index[current−1..current+2] and a tick-scheduled try_commit independent of add_vertex. Add a test with an observer node that drops one vertex and asserts WANTED is populated and the hole admitted with zero inbound DAG_VERTEX traffic.
titles: Fetch trigger is proposer-only and try_commit is inbound-driven: observers, jailed validators and partitioned nodes never populate WANTED, and E2's 'defer and WANTED' is never re-evaluated without traffic (I6/I14 recur)

claim: Sync-settlement release is keyed through WANTED[H].blocked, so a hash settling after its entry expired is never released
sections: §5.5 Release, §3 cache invalidation rule (b), §5.2 TTL/quota/`> current+2` exclusions, §8
attacks: Restart case from the previous hole with ChainSync ON but slow on the first pass (initial `sync_from_peers` waits 3 s, tip agreement, batch of 500 blocks executed synchronously in `process_blocks`). Tick t: proposer walk WANTs the pruned band hashes H_1..H_k; all peers answer `unknown`; entries carry `blocked = {C_1..C_n}` (the round-(current−1) candidates). Tick t+64: TTL evicts WANTED[H_i] (§5.2 'receiver-tick TTL of 64 ticks regardless of tier'). Tick t+70: `reload_chain_tip` adopts the synced blocks; `committed_set` now contains H_1..H_k. §5.5 release runs 'On … sync settlement of H: remove WANTED[H], invalidate resolved entries listed in blocked' — WANTED[H] no longer exists, so no `blocked` list, so no invalidation; the cache still holds `Unresolved{blocked_on ⊇ H_i}` for C_1..C_n and for every intermediate vertex the walk cached on the way down. If `resolve_walk` short-circuits on a cached `Unresolved` sub-entry (the only way the stated bound 'n walks per tick' is cheaper than n × full-cone re-descents at n=100), then every later candidate whose cone passes through those vertices inherits the stale verdict, (c) re-walks the top-level candidate but hits the same stale sub-entries, and the node never resolves > 2/3 again. The same gap exists for hashes that never entered WANTED because of the Tier A budget (256), the per-author quota, or the `> current_round + 2` exclusion.
fixes: Keep the reverse index `blocked_on → {dependent vertex hashes}` inside the `resolved` cache itself (Part I already needs it for rule (b), which has no WANTED), and have the sync hook iterate `block.committed_vertices` against THAT index; WANTED removal is a side effect, not the key. Specify explicitly that `resolve_walk` never short-circuits on a cached `Unresolved` sub-entry unless that entry's `blocked_on` hashes are all still absent from `dag ∪ shadow ∪ committed_set` (a cheap O(|blocked_on|) recheck), so a stale verdict can never survive a settlement it missed. Add a mutation row: 'TTL-expire WANTED before adoption; assert candidates re-resolve after adoption with 0 add_vertex calls' (extends `sync_settlement_rewalks_blocked`).
titles: Sync-settlement release is keyed through WANTED[H].blocked; a hash that settles after its WANTED entry expired (or was never created) invalidates nothing, and the design leaves open whether a stale `Unresolved` cache entry short-circuits descendant walks
